No. 01 — The point of viewEditor’s noteMedLifeOfMushi · Made for Med Minds.
01 / The point of view

Medicine,
made legible.

An independent learning desk, written by a student, for students.

MedLifeOfMushi is an independent learning desk for the next generation of healthcare professionals. We bring the scattered parts of medical student life into one considered space: practical study systems, carefully structured resources, clinical foundations and opportunities worth your attention.

It is written from inside the classroom, by a second-year BHMS student. That means two lenses, side by side: the conventional medical sciences, and the homoeopathic system taught alongside them. Wherever the homoeopathic perspective appears, it is marked with a bottle, so you always know which lens you are reading through.

Less noise. Better questions. A clearer connection between what you learn and how medicine works.

“Medicine, make it make sense.”

— The editor, MedLifeOfMushi

No. 05 — The Homoeopathic LensA second way of lookingTraditional teaching, clearly labelled
02.3 / Through the homoeopathic lens

The homoeopathic
lens.

Every BHMS student reads medicine in two languages at once.

Alongside anatomy, physiology and pathology sits the system built on Hahnemann’s Organon of Medicine. On this site, whenever a card, case or subject is explained through that system, you will see the bottle. These are the ideas it is built on, as they are taught in the curriculum.

01Similia similibus curentur“Let like be treated by like.”
02Totality of symptomsThe whole person, not one complaint.
03IndividualisationTwo patients, one diagnosis, two pictures.
04Drug provingRemedies studied on healthy volunteers.
05Minimum dosePotentisation by serial dilution and succussion.
06The vital forceHahnemann’s dynamis, disturbed in disease.
Read this carefully. This is traditional teaching, kept separate from established scientific evidence. Systematic reviews have not shown homoeopathy to work better than placebo for any condition. It is presented here as the system is taught for the BHMS course, for study, and is not medical advice.
